technical_and_design_decisions: Treat the increment as work on the existing legacy XD/s-c-s codebase represented by the user stories, rather than upgrading the entire system to Spring Framework 6 or Java 17.
Preserve existing public module, channel, deployment, and configuration contracts unless required by the user stories.
Move Kafka and Rabbit sink modules into the target s-c-s repository as first-class modules, reusing existing messaging abstractions and build conventions where possible.
Implement per-channel binder selection through explicit channel-level configuration, with a default binder retained for backward compatibility.
Use an external, precedence-ordered configuration file that overrides packaged defaults, including module coordinates and module resolution properties.
Refactor the Cloud Foundry SPI deployer behind the existing deployer abstraction and use the selected CF Java client as the implementation boundary.
Represent Hadoop distribution selection as a validated configuration option mapped to distribution-specific classpath and dependency sets.
Move header-enricher source and tests into XD proper while preserving its runtime behavior and user-facing configuration.
Perform the specified Spring Integration, Spring Framework, and AMQP dependency upgrades together, resolving compatibility issues without broad unrelated dependency modernization.
Use automated unit, integration, build, and compatibility tests as the primary verification mechanism, with representative Kafka, Rabbit, Redis, Cloud Foundry, and Hadoop configurations.
assumptions: The existing repositories, build system, CI infrastructure, and representative test environments are available and can be modified by one developer.

The Kafka, Rabbit, header-enricher, deployer, and Hadoop implementations already exist in source form or have sufficiently complete equivalents to migrate; this estimate excludes creating entirely new messaging implementations.
Kafka, Rabbit, and Redis broker services can be run locally or through existing test infrastructure; provisioning new shared environments is excluded.
The CF Java client version and API are compatible with the supported Cloud Foundry API, and the refactor does not require changes to the Cloud Foundry server.
Hadoop distribution support is limited to selecting among a defined set of existing distributions and dependency/classpath mappings, not implementing distribution-specific runtime behavior.
External configuration is file-based and loaded at application startup; live reload, configuration-server integration, and a new administration UI are excluded.
The dependency upgrade targets are the versions stated in U8, and the current product branch can remain on its existing Java baseline despite the general Spring Framework background text.
Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation, and CI/build updates, but excludes project management, release operations, and extended production support.
One workday represents approximately eight hours of focused development effort; the estimates measure effort rather than elapsed calendar time.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing XD and s-c-s repository structure, module build conventions, binder architecture, deployment SPI, configuration loading, dependency graph, test strategy, and migration constraints. Produce the detailed implementation plan and identify compatibility risks.

Migrate the Kafka module from XD into the s-c-s repository, adapt package and build metadata, connect it to the target module and binder abstractions, preserve sink configuration and serialization behavior, and add or migrate unit and integration tests.

Migrate the Rabbit module from XD into the s-c-s repository, adapt dependencies and packaging, integrate it with the target module and binder abstractions, preserve sink behavior and configuration, and add or migrate unit and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Implement different binder types per channel
activities.activity_description: Extend channel and module configuration models to support channel-level binder selection, resolve binder instances by name or type, retain default-binder behavior for existing applications, validate invalid combinations, and test Rabbit, Redis, and Kafka as source or sink binders.

Add external configuration file discovery, parsing, precedence, validation, and merge behavior for module defaults and overrides, including alternate Maven coordinates and module resolution. Update startup errors, configuration documentation, and automated tests.

Analyze the existing Cloud Foundry deployer SPI, introduce or adapt a clean client-facing abstraction, replace direct or outdated implementation details with the CF Java client, preserve deployment operations and error handling, and add unit and integration coverage for the refactored behavior.

Define the supported Hadoop distribution option, validate configuration, map each option to the appropriate Hadoop libraries and classpath entries, preserve the default behavior, and test dependency/classpath resolution for each supported distribution.

Relocate the header-enricher implementation, metadata, configuration, resources, and tests from the modules repository into XD proper. Update registration, packaging, documentation, and compatibility tests while removing obsolete references.

activities.activity_name: Upgrade Spring Integration, Spring Framework, and AMQP dependencies
activities.activity_description: Update dependencies to Spring Integration 4.2, Spring Framework 4.2.1, and AMQP 1.5, resolve API and transitive dependency changes, update affected code and tests, and verify startup and representative messaging flows.

Run the complete build and regression suite, add end-to-end pipeline coverage combining channel-specific binders with migrated sinks, verify external overrides and Hadoop selection, test deployer compatibility, and diagnose and fix integration defects.

activities.activity_name: Documentation, CI, packaging, and delivery preparation
activities.activity_description: Update user and developer documentation, configuration examples, migration notes, repository manifests, build and CI jobs, release metadata, and final packaging. Perform a clean checkout verification and prepare the completed increment for review and release.
